title: The Danger of Being Easily Offended
summaryZh: 拒絕冒犯能保護我們的心思；悔改是重新對齊神看事情的眼光，使我們成為活祭。
lines: I can still see his face.
"I give up my right to be offended."
Honestly, I've tried to take it a step farther.
老實說，我試著更進一步。
In cases like this, I pray for great mercy, great grace.
在這種情況下，我祈求極大的憐憫和極大的恩典。
But the point is, I don't want the poison of offense to cloud my vision.
但重點是，我不希望冒犯的毒根蒙蔽我的眼光。
I don't want it to affect my thinking, my reasoning, because it does.
我不希望它影響我的思考和理智，因為它確實會。
The target is to get offense, to get bitterness, envy, any of these things, to get it somewhere influencing the reasoning.
它的目標是要讓冒犯、苦毒、嫉妒或任何這些東西，進入某處去影響我們的理智。
So that I'm not able to demonstrate the heart of God on planet Earth in the measure He desires.
好讓我無法在地球上，按著神所渴望的程度，來彰顯祂的心意。
So I want you to look with me at Romans 12, and we'll take this for the remaining part of the morning.
所以我想請你們和我一起看羅馬書 12 章，我們早上剩下的時間就來講這段。
I don't know what I'd do if you said no, but I do prefer people surviving the meeting.
我不知道如果你們說沒有我該怎麼辦，但我確實希望大家能撐過這場聚會。

Verse 1 of chapter 12, Romans 12: "I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that you present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable to God, which is your reasonable service."
羅馬書 12 章第 1 節：「所以弟兄們，我以神的慈悲勸你們，將身體獻上，當作活祭，是聖潔的，是神所喜悅的；你們如此事奉乃是理所當然的。」
I think one of the translations, maybe New American, says, "reasonable service of worship."
我想有一個譯本，也許是新美國標準譯本，說的是「理所當然的敬拜事奉」。
Present your bodies a living sacrifice, your reasonable service.
將身體獻上，當作活祭，你們理所當然的事奉。
Becoming a living offering is the intellectual thing to do.
成為一個活祭是明智之舉。
Have you discovered yet that God thinks different than you?
你發現了嗎？神思考的方式和你不同。
Guess who's not going to change?
What repentance does is it re-engages with the way He thinks.
悔改的作用，就是重新接上祂思考的方式。
Repentance is reconnecting with the perception of God regarding a matter.
悔改是重新連結神對某件事的看法。
Most of our lives are spent in the middle of challenges, difficulties, problems, victories, whatever it might be.
我們生命中大部分的時間都花在面對挑戰、困難、問題或勝利，不管那是什麼。
And in the middle of these issues, we are crying out to God for Him to come and help, and to fix the situation.
在這些問題當中，我們呼求神來幫助，並解決這景況。
But Jesus modeled a different way of living.
但耶穌示範了另一種不同的生活方式。
I hope that we can come into this instruction and experience more thoroughly in the next couple of years.
我希望在接下來的幾年裡，我們能更透徹地進入這項教導和經歷中。
Yeah, I'm so glad that you watched this video.
是的，我很高興你們看了這支影片。
I do pray that it's a great strength and encouragement to you.
我真誠地祈求這對你們是極大的力量和鼓勵。
And I've got a verse that really is my cry for all of us, and it's Psalms 20, it's verse 4:
我有一節經文，真的是我為我們大家的呼求，那就是詩篇 20 篇，第 4 節：
"May He grant you your heart's desire and fulfill all your plans."
「將你心所願的賜給你，成就你的一切籌算。」
That's my prayer, that this would be a season of rich fulfillment.
那是我的禱告，願這是一個經歷豐富成就的季節。
